DrugAnalysis.title: DrugAnalysis — FDA Decisions & Biotech Reactions
DrugAnalysis.description: Biopharma decision engine tracking publicly traded companies against FDA drug decisions, verified stock-price reactions and clinical-pipeline success rates, rendered as a dependency-free static site with no build step. Latest state read from the repository (v27, 2026-09-21): 1,000 new verified FDA decision rows for 2000-2026 (38 in 2000 then 37 per year through 2026), every field taken verbatim from 27 committed, SHA-checked openFDA payload files holding 2,969 decisions, with a Drugs@FDA URL, a replayable openFDA query and the payload file plus SHA prefix on every row, and the ticker left blank rather than guessed unless an exact SEC registry match exists. Alongside it: a 27-row year-by-year table giving the openFDA ORIG/AP count per year against the v27 selected count with Type 1-5 and Priority/Standard breakdowns; a 1,933-row decision engine analysis table joining company, clinical trial result, FDA decision, before/after and T+1 stock pricing and a company success-rate summary with no estimation; a 485-row company success-rate scorecard scoring pipeline progression 0-100 with an A-E grade; a 2,848-row stock-price verified index carrying Yahoo chart API and manual verification URLs per row; and an 18-factor decision-factors table in which every multiplier cites its source, including BIO/Biomedtracker base rates (90.6% Phase 1 to 2 on n=1453, 57.8% Phase 3 to NDA, 52.4% likelihood of approval) and FDA pathway and advisory-committee guidance. The historical layers stand: a 1,215-row full submission register for 1938-1964 covering non-approval decision types, the v26 census of 535 original approvals for 1939-1964 verified by 16,157 independent checks with 0 errors, and a verified-negative determination for 1938 itself — 0 submissions in the official database window, so no row is invented. scripts/validate_data.py reports PASS with 0 errors.

GEMSDOE.title: GEMSDOE — Geologic Mapping Prize Challenge
GEMSDOE.description: Evidence-backed site for the DOE GEMS Prize Challenge on DrivenData ($300,000 total prize — $50k initial, $250k final — ending 2026-12-03): predicting geothermal faults in the GeoDAWN region under a distance-weighted Tversky metric, with a 19-band feature stack. Session-19 status read from STATUS.md: all four block-holdout folds are now committed and the memorisation-vs-transfer gap is reported as a spread rather than a point — fold 0 +0.0114, fold 1 −0.0070, fold 2 +0.0139, fold 3 +0.0093, mean +0.006904, spread 0.020935, positive in 3 of 4 — and because no fold reaches the ≥12 resampling units a readable block-bootstrap interval needs, the scorer itself flags every per-fold interval `interval_readable: false`, so the honest reading is 'no clear memorisation, no clear transfer gain' with the full-grid 0.099859 (reproduced digit-for-digit on a runner) retained as the selection statistic. The pseudo-label contrast is measured on every committed truth population and points in opposite directions on the two components, but it has now FIRED TWICE and STATUS.md is explicit that 'quoting either one alone would overstate the precision'. The first fire gave held-out blocks 0.0806 → 0.1841 (+0.1036, P=0.999) on the new-fault-like proxy against 0.2113 → 0.1239 (−0.0874, P=0.001) on catalogue labels, deriving TRADE_OFF_PROXY_GAINS_CATALOGUE_LOSSES; the second fire — same seed, same config, same partition, different runner — measured proxy +0.0677 and catalogue −0.1079, deriving GAIN_ON_THE_COMBINED_SURROGATE. That is a ~0.036 run-to-run swing on the proxy arm, the same order of magnitude as the +0.0313 union contrast itself, and the two scopes disagree in sign on the union (+0.0313 held-out against −0.0375 trained-on), which STATUS.md calls instability rather than a result. Read against the bar its own FIELD rule uses (paired block bootstrap P ≥ 0.95), the union contrast reaches P = 0.916 with an interval spanning zero on 8 scoreable blocks, so it is suggestive and not established; both fires' numbers remain in git history but the second overwrote the first's committed evidence files. Both verdicts carry `shippable_evidence: false`, and the circularity is derived rather than asserted, because the pseudo-label path is the same proxy_catalogue.tif the proxy truth is cut from. STATUS.md also defuses one coincidence on purpose: the baseline's union held-out DTI of 0.197183 resembles the public leaderboard's top score of 0.1972, and the two are unrelated quantities. A third population, the disjoint 122,652-pixel union (60,988 + 61,664, disjointness verified at score time), scores the shipped artifact 0.207431 CI95 [0.192924, 0.222879] and puts the adopted emission policy 2nd of 10 distinct emissions (50 swept, 40 pruned as duplicates) — the 1-pixel widening that beats it scores +0.0054 at P=0.815, below both pre-registered bars (P ≥ 0.95 and +0.010), so the adopted policy holds on a third population too, while the union arm that landed as run 35477119490 is recorded as suggestive, under-powered and not shippable. Session 18's pre-registered FIELD-selection rule (docs/FIELD_SELECTION_RULE.md), machine-gated first in reblend.yml, still returns KEEP mean12. Session 21 (2026-09-21) closed the standing data-placement blocker inside a sandbox: scripts/assemble_data_bridge.py reassembled all three official rasters from committed parts in 2.8 s, verifying every part sha256 and each whole-file sha256 against data/bridge/manifest.json (training_features.tif 418,912,844 B, labels.tif 425,830 B, sample_submission.tif 1,599,597 B), after which prepare_data.py PASSED on the placed bytes (3292x3730, 19 bands, EPSG:32611, 100 m, aligned bounds, band tags present). The CPU-only route to a submission was then re-executed end to end and reproduced the committed artifact byte for byte — the same selected policy (floor 0.000974, thin, width 0 px, union DTI 0.160259 on selection fold 0) and a submission.tif whose sha256 matches the committed baseline, with the generalisation audit re-scoring untouched fold 1 at catalogue 0.06597 / proxy 0.071107 / combined 0.078916, reproduced=True and max absolute delta 0.00016874; the two reports differ only in timings. validate_submission.py passed all 8 checks on the freshly written file, and the pre-registered support cap did its job visibly by excluding the highest-scoring candidate (floor 0.009487, union 0.197198) for emitting 487,813 px, 9.4% of the footprint, with the reason printed in the report. The submission subpage's claims were re-read line by line against the official problem description and competition home and hold.

GitHub has not recomputed it since despite roughly 180,000 lines of new JSON evidence landing in session 19, which is the asynchronous-`size` behaviour IRR-04 to IRR-06 describe.

MasterSite.title: MasterSite — Master GitHub Pages Directory
MasterSite.description: This site: the master directory and line-by-line verification ledger for every GitHub Pages site published under buffedlizard55-lab, plus a verified check of kanlerxz87-cyber. Each of the 63 entries carries a sourced description, creation date, last-updated date, commit telemetry, Pages build source, the commit its prose was read at, and official API links for independent manual review. Two views — a card grid and a table — are retuned by a per-browser Density preference: the table is compact by default because its job is comparison, dropping rows from about 60px to about 29px with a fixed-width name column and the curated title clipped to one line, and below 900px the same nine cells re-stack into labelled lines so a phone reads a card per site instead of scrolling a ~1,000px table sideways. That narrow-screen layout is CSS only: the DOM keeps nine cells in the same order at every width, the column headings stay in the accessibility tree, and the colspan=9 empty state is unchanged, which is what tests/directory.spec.js asserts along with horizontal-fit at 375px, the export equality of the JSON and CSV downloads and the exact reset-filter URL. Filtering, sorting, search, the inspector dialog and both exports are client-side over a single generated data file. Nothing here is hand-entered: data/sites.js is produced by tools/build_data.py from the GitHub REST API plus tools/overlay.json for narrative, VERIFICATION.md is produced by tools/build_verification.py from that, and four read-only tools — verify_live.py, audit_descriptions.py, audit_kind.py and the generator's own prose gate — re-check the published claims against the repositories every pass. Their results are published whether or not they are flattering, including the entries whose prose is provably behind their repository head.

NFLInjuryReport.title: NFL Injury Report — 32 Team Tracker
NFLInjuryReport.description: Live injury-alert system for all 32 NFL teams built only from free, public, verifiable sources: every designation shown is the official nfl.com value whenever nfl.com publishes one, with ESPN's keyless injuries JSON supplying timestamps and beat-writer attribution, plus a reporter-accuracy scorecard and a chat-style live feed. Player positions are now displayed across the live feed, alerts and reports, read from the ESPN feed's athlete.position.abbreviation field. A GitHub Actions workflow refreshes data/latest/*.json every 10 minutes and commits it to the branch; the Pages site is the repository root with no build step. The repository documents the limits of the scorecard honestly: a historical backfill is not achievable from free sources because no keyless archive of historical social posts with trustworthy timestamps exists (and the official side has had no free read tier since February 2026), so scoring is forward-collected from the moment the collector is enabled.

StockPaperSim.title: StockPaperSim — Persona Paper-Trading Competition (Replay + Live Book)
StockPaperSim.description: One-year paper-trading competition between return-seeking strategy personas, with a real venue model (depth, spreads, market making, dated tick sizes and fees), a full audit trail and a dependency-free static site. The repository documents three runs, re-read 2026-09-20 at its fourth pass: Season 1 with 20 personas replaying the real S&P 500 and VIX path (republished with its numbers re-derived rather than patched), the legacy Live Book with 19 personas trading forward from official free series (Nasdaq Composite, Dow Jones, S&P 500, VIX, SOFR and four macro series), and Season 2 with 19 personas in a reproducible research replay on collected daily bars — the Season 2 roster having grown from 14 to 19 with three new slate personas (NFL, NBA, NCAA) and two forward-only probes, while the landed complete ESPN NBA scoreboard (1,330 rows, 2025-10-21 to 2026-06-14) lets the NBA slate persona trade the full 2025-26 season. The fourth pass is the arrival of real SEC Form 4 insider data through an agent lane: a rendered-extraction campaign collected 65 filings and 99 parsed transactions across all ten tracked tickers (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, JPM, XOM, JNJ, PG, TSLA, MU, T), every filing dated on or after 2026-06-01, captured as the SEC's own XSL-rendered Form 4 views plus filing indexes through the page-fetch route into data/real/sec_agent/, whose 131-entry staged_manifest.json has every file SHA-256 digested and re-verified at staging. sim/edgar_rendered.py parses those captures fail-closed — handling footnoted codes and prices, dual and triple checkbox roles and 10b5-1 plan flags — and scripts/stage_sec_rendered.py integrates the lane into the same JSONL the walk and bulk sets feed, de-duplicated on (accession, date, ticker, code, shares, price). Commodities.title: Commodities — Kalshi Research Exchange
Commodities.description: Evidence-first paper-trading lab for Kalshi event contracts, organised around an automated forward-test desk. 23 return-seeking strategy personas (plus 4 gated ones) trade open Kalshi contracts on paper twice an hour from a scheduled, read-only GitHub Actions collector, and every fill, exit, settlement, intent, mark and order book is committed back to the repository. Two backtests run on verified official Kalshi price data: the original hand-collected sample (3 settled markets, 130 verified bars, 5 personas), deliberately frozen, and an archive backtest replayed bar by bar over the candle archive the collector now stores (45 markets, 1,691 verified bars, 199 trades, 9 rule sets, with per-trade equity curves and a walk-forward stability split). An execution-realism check re-reads every simulated fill against Kalshi's own published trade tape via GET /markets/trades and reports the difference in cents, with a committed live result of 158 fills compared at a median absolute desk-minus-tape gap of 1.00 cent. A season health audit (scripts/audit_season.py) checks the schedule, ledger coverage, storage compaction, signal adapters and the tape summary, re-reads settled markets against the official API on the runner, and refuses to let verify_data.py pass if anything disagrees. Simulation only: nothing submits orders to Kalshi and no API key exists anywhere in the project.

OLBG-Competition.title: Northstar Competition Lab — OLBG Tipster Paper Trading
OLBG-Competition.description: A deliberately small, evidence-first betting-research workbench whose central finding is that none of its strategies beat the market on the pilot sample. Sport two is ice hockey (DEL 2024/25) on the same open-licensed OpenLigaDB path, with overtime- and shootout-aware final-score selection and one Elo strategy that produces predictions only: 11 graded predictions, 7 correct (63.6%), Brier 0.4737, and PnL reported as unavailable rather than zero because no permissioned odds path exists for hockey. Sport three is darts (PDC), prediction-only, where the cold 2025 pool made 0 selections in 141 opportunities because the maximum probability of 0.551 never cleared the 0.60 threshold — recorded as silence with no refit — while the full 2025-26 pool graded 39 of 48 correct (81.25%) at Brier 0.349. Identity is labelled per sport: football verified, hockey and darts probable on a single source. 258 offline pytest tests cover fixtures, odds parsing, time-zone handling, settlement, walk-forward invariants and each pilot's guarantees, and every number carries a licence and a retrieval date with the ODbL attribution for OpenLigaDB stated on the site itself.

ShoulderPain.title: ShoulderPain — Research-Backed Shoulder & Scapula Pain Guide
ShoulderPain.description: Source-linked GitHub Pages guide to shoulder and shoulder-blade ('wing') pain, written around one stated context — a male adult aged about 36-40, left-side sleeping, a possible workout injury, prolonged computer use and limited room space — and explicitly educational information rather than a diagnosis or a personalised rehabilitation plan, with emergency and urgent warning signs given priority over exercises, furniture or symptom logging. Ten pages share one static template and compact navigation: start, medical advice, treatment, exercises, desk and room, furniture and prices, care costs, an optional log, sources and audit, and next steps; all research content works without JavaScript and no sign-in or symptom entry is required. The current revision is a deliberate narrowing rather than an expansion. It reviewed the pre-existing site at commit e1c63c4 and, in its own words, 'replaces blanket verification/completeness claims with a narrower, auditable source register, simplifies the UI and corrects unsafe or unverified assumptions', keeping the previous site in Git history. Twenty official pages were opened directly on 2026-09-20 — MedlinePlus, NHS, AAOS/ASES, CSP, OSHA, CMS, five furniture manufacturers or sellers, and Luna — and data/sources.json records each source's section, a short excerpt, its scope and its check date, with government and medical-society guidance kept separate from commercial product information. data/claims.json maps source-bearing content units to references and source-file lines: 90 review units, described as a review aid and 'not an automated truth certificate'. Exercises were reduced to four source-checked examples carrying exact AAOS HTML doses and supervision boundaries. Five furniture listings give exact variant and price boundaries with folding trade-offs, and no product is claimed to fit an unmeasured room or to treat shoulder pain; the one care price quoted is an official provider example ($135 self-pay per visit at Luna), not a nationwide average, and other unverified medical costs are explicitly left unpriced. REVIEW.md documents three passes and eight source irregularities found while reading, including a COMHOMA price where $54.49 was the selected White variant and $25.50 the discount, a VIVO desk that folds against the wall but is not quickly detached, a Lillipad whose specifications claim a 700 lb static test while its FAQ says 350 lb and neither replaces the 75 lb operational rating, and a Luna search excerpt showing $125 where both directly opened pages showed $135. The optional log is local-only, retains the `shoulderpain-log-v1` key so prior entries can still be read or imported if valid, and validates numbers, booleans, calendar dates and shape; invalid entries are counted and never rounded or silently converted, invalid persisted data blocks edits rather than being overwritten, raw JSON export is available for recovery, cross-tab changes block saves until reload, spreadsheet formula injection is mitigated on CSV export, and the bounded import size was raised to 20 MB so the 5,000-entry schema can import its own backups. Its former clinical 'improving/worsening' classifier and calendar-based advice were removed on the grounds that sparse logs should not reassure someone or postpone assessment, and the summary is now descriptive only. Validation reports 8 Node unit tests and 31 Chromium browser tests passing, automated axe WCAG 2 A/AA and 2.1 AA checks passing on all ten pages at 390px and 1440px, and no page-level horizontal overflow at 320, 390, 768 or 1440px. Sources retrieved 2026-09-20.
flags: Its own verification policy refuses the strongest claims a directory reader might assume: 'Unknown or conflicting facts stay visibly unresolved. No claim of independent clinical verification or zero errors', and 'Automated checks cannot establish medical accuracy'. REVIEW.md adds that no clinician independently reviewed the personalised suitability of the information, and that link integrity, automated accessibility and browser tests are not medical validation.

Deliberately narrower than the version it replaced. The prior revision carried a 56-source register (S1-S56), four logged review passes, 32 logged corrections and a 32-row irregularity table; this one carries 20 opened sources, three passes, 8 source irregularities and a 6-row next-steps table. Its stated reason is worth quoting because it is the opposite of the usual instinct: 'The guide is a focused, source-linked starting set, not all possible diseases or products. Further expansion should improve evidence rather than inflate a count' (IRR-57).

Now has a build and test step, unlike the version previously described here: npm ci, npm run build (claim ledger plus ten static root HTML pages), npm run check, npm test, npm run test:browser (Playwright) and npm run serve, with the shared page layout in tools/build.py and Python 3 and Node 22 used in validation. Visitors need neither. Committed root HTML means the Pages configuration needs no runtime build.

Browser tests were run against an npm-distributed Chromium 153 binary extracted outside Git because the standard Playwright browser download and Debian package retrieval were blocked by sandbox networking; REVIEW.md states plainly that 'this is not an unexecuted test claim', and CI uses the normal Playwright installation on GitHub-hosted runners. Remaining testing limits it names: no manual screen-reader-user audit, no cross-browser matrix, no third-party video-playback test, and automated accessibility is not full conformance certification.

Open limitations it lists for a next session: no clinician exam or clinical peer review and no systematic literature review; actual room fit, safe removal route and body/desk measurements unknown; no checked chair meets both the folding and the adjustable long-day-workstation criteria; product stock, prices and return policies change and Lillipad has contradictory page content; personal care and medicine costs, country and insurance remain unknown.

Changed state four times inside one audit and this description is the fourth rewrite — verified in sequence against 239eaa8 (01:25:47Z), dd1a7d4 (02:13:17Z), 6812ef3 (02:42:19Z, 60 seconds after a prior stamp had been written) and now 8a21b94 (03:07:51Z), which rebuilt all ten pages and reversed the sourcing method entirely (IRR-47, IRR-57).

Re-verified upstream on 21 September 2026: every medical, exercise and workstation source (M1-M6, E1-E3, W1-W3) was re-opened and all registered excerpts still match the official pages. Product rechecks succeeded only partially — VIVO and Lillipad were re-verified through official seller product-data endpoints, while fetch-proxy failures prevented re-opening IKEA, Branch, three manual/spec PDFs and the cost sources, whose entries stay dated 20 September 2026 and are labelled as such on the site. No price, stock or fit fact was invented for the items that could not be re-opened.

VacationSchedule.title: VacationSchedule — Free Time Scoreboard (SF Radio Blackout Calendar)
VacationSchedule.description: Bay Area vacation planner comparing three definitions of sports-free time in 2026-2029 for a listener in San Francisco ZIP 94122, with one-, two- and three-week trip checks, a daily scoreboard, a month calendar, Pacific-time free intervals, sources and a review queue. The three sections nest: Section 1 counts all 30 MLB clubs plus 49ers preseason, regular season and postseason and the Westwood One national NFL feeds as busy; Section 2 adds Stanford and California football; Section 3 adds San Jose Earthquakes MLS. An 'Everything tracked' option adds national NCAA football plus Golden State Warriors and Golden State Valkyries on KGMZ 95.7 The Game. Only AM/FM broadcasts count, so the San Jose Sharks (app/streaming only) and Audacy-app-only Valkyries games are disclosed exclusions, and USF basketball, Westwood One NCAA basketball and local college basketball are named as documented gaps rather than silently treated as free time. With Spring Training excluded, Sections 1 and 2 give longest modeled windows of 44 days in 2026 (Feb 9 - Mar 24, past), 37 in 2027 (Feb 15 - Mar 23), 40 in 2028 (estimated) and 41 in 2029 (estimated); with Spring Training included no section reaches two weeks. The repository refuses a blanket verified claim: TBD kickoff reserves the entire local date including DST 23- and 25-hour days, 'no known conflict' is stated to describe the snapshot rather than certify a quiet day, and all times are America/Los_Angeles rather than a fixed UTC-8 offset. A 2026-09-21 session-3 pass added two tabs: MLB 2026 & 2027, listing every fixture the league has scheduled for all 30 clubs from the committed Stats API snapshot with each row carrying the league's own game_pk, and Postseason 2026, which splits the postseason into what is resolved and what is not — clinched berths and division titles, official round dates, dates that cannot carry a game, and a machine-measured count of published first pitches, still zero. The fixture lists are produced on a GitHub runner by scripts/export_mlb_schedule.py, validated for all 30 clubs, a plausible regular-season count and unique game ids, and committed with a provenance summary recording the exact request URL, the retrieval time and a SHA-256 of the raw response, so every row is re-verifiable by hand. MLBComp.title: MLBComp — Auditable MLB Research & Paper Competition
MLBComp.description: Auditable MLB research and paper-betting platform running the loop research -> discover -> verify -> model -> backtest -> forward-test -> paper trade -> analyze -> improve, with no bookmaker, exchange or order-placement client anywhere in the repository. It separates REG, POST, WC, DS, LCS and WS environments (ALL is a roll-up view, not a blended score), carries 68 versioned strategy hypotheses with immutable strategy and model version records, and keeps an append-only SHA-256 hash-chained ledger protected by SQLite UPDATE and DELETE triggers. MLBRainDelay.title: MLB Rain Delay — Live Scoreboard with Weather & Delay Tracking

SelfLearn.title: SelfLearn — Autonomous No-LLM Research Engine
SelfLearn.description: Autonomous research engine that will not publish a sentence it cannot quote from a document it actually retrieved, and that contains no language model anywhere in its pipeline: claims are spans cut out of retrieved documents and accepted or rejected by string and set operations anyone can re-run. It has no third-party dependencies at all, not even for HTTP or HTML, and requires Python 3.10 or newer. One cycle plans what to read, retrieves through a politeness- and budget-limited client, hashes and stores the response in evidence/snapshots/ before anything reads it, cuts candidate claims, verifies each against the stored document (numbers, dates, polarity, direction, universality, then quote match and token coverage), detects contradictions, lets six competing personas build answers out of verified claims only, attacks them with eleven named deterministic critic rules, ranks them on nine published criteria with Elo ratings accumulating across cycles, runs seeded experiments in a subprocess with a tamper check on the script hash, derives new questions and publishes everything as a static site plus machine-readable JSON. Library state read from reports/site_data.json at commit b787077 (generated 2026-09-22T23:12:31Z): 300 claims, 89 documents, 222 competing candidates carrying 960 recorded criticisms, 141 derived open questions, 12 contradictions awaiting a human decision, 102 discoveries, 4 topics, 22 recorded failures and 35 registered irregularities — 28 open (15 warning, 13 info, 0 error) and 7 resolved. The 156-test suite was executed in this audit and passed.

MasterSelfLearn.title: MasterSelfLearn — Autonomous Evidence-First Research Engine

A cycle is seven stages, each a separate module that can fail without stopping the others — a failed stage becomes an entry in the irregularity register and the cycle still publishes. FLABSENGY.title: FLABSENGY — FantasyLabs Projection Reverse Engineering
FLABSENGY.description: Clean-room study of the FantasyLabs DFS projection system plus an original Python engine that rebuilds the metrics the vendor documents publicly — no subscription data, no scraped pages, no proprietary weights, and an explicit record of what was refused. Evidence counted at commit f927bab: docs/ledger.html holds 49 source rows inside an S1-S50 range, research/IRREGULARITIES.md carries 16 flagged items I1-I16, research/REQUIREMENTS.md maps acceptance requirements R1-R17, and engine/fantasylab_engine/metrics.py defines 14 functions covering Plus/Minus, implied points from a salary-expectation fit, Pts/Sal, consistency, upside, duds, bargain rating, opponent Plus/Minus, salary change and percentile rank. `pytest -q` was executed in this audit and returned 79 passed. Where the vendor's own official glossaries disagree — the NFL defines Duds as fewer than half a salary-based expectation while the NBA and MLB glossaries define it as at least half a standard deviation below it — the engine implements both variants and documents which one is the default; where a methodology is not public at all (ownership projection, Pro Trend definitions, salary-regression parameters) it is recorded as unknown rather than guessed.

ParlaySports.title: ParlaySports — Multi-Sport Parlay Paper Competition
ParlaySports.description: Simulated multi-sport parlay research platform and paper-trading competition across NFL, MLB, NHL and NBA — dependency-free Python engine, hash-routed static site, two sealed books that are accounted separately and never merged. State read from data/site/meta.json at commit f939267 (engine 1.1.0, exported 2026-09-22T20:06:21Z over data as of 2026-09-22T01:30:00Z): 29,056 games, 7,014 parlays, 20,570 legs and the same 20,570 signals, 8,267 ledger rows, 60,504 prices, 54,296 ratings, 28 strategies, 28 users, 24 research items, 28 verifications and 13 open quality issues. The catalog in parlaysports/strategies.py is 28 versioned strategies — six per sport plus four multi-sport — each with a named manager, a written hypothesis, selection rules, a minimum edge and documented limitations, staking 10 USD per ticket (the longshot lottery book 25 USD) from a 10,000 USD bankroll per strategy per book. Every leg and ticket carries a pricing grade: VERIFIED, REFERENCE, MODEL, MIXED or UNPRICED, the last tracked for hit rate only at 0 stake. Settlement is append-only from final scores, with push and void legs reducing a ticket and an all-push ticket refunded. Three gates were executed in this audit rather than quoted: the unittest suite ran 60 tests OK, the committed data/audit_report.json holds 63 checks every one of which is PASS, and node scripts/ui_smoke.mjs rendered all 15 site routes.
flags: The committed audit report is 63/63 PASS, but re-running scripts/audit.py from a fresh clone in this audit stopped at check 2 with 'database-exists: run seed first', because the working database is not committed. The 63/63 published here is the repository's own persisted record at this commit, not a gate this audit reproduced end to end; `make seed` has to run first. IRR-78.

Coverage gaps are declared rather than padded: the pinned MLB results file holds full 2023-2025 and Apr-Jul 2015 only, with nothing for 2016-2022, so MLB backtests run over 2023-2025 and a missing-historical-periods quality check flags the gap on every build. NBA backtests use Oct-Dec slices only from the SBR archive, S-NHL-05 has no verified puck-line history and is forward-armed only, S-MLB-06 is forward-only by design, and multi-sport backtests cover only measured cross-sport overlap slates.

MODEL-grade payouts are estimates from assumed -110 or proxy lines and are labelled as such; backtests assume closing-line availability and ignore line movement, limits and fees; multi-sport legs assume independence with no correlation model and there are no same-game parlays in v1; Kalshi prices exclude exchange fees; and player and game props are not simulated at all because no free verified historical prop feed exists.

Twelve inherited NBA rows were 0-0 'finals' for games that had been postponed: nine are verified against published postponement notices and three are recorded as not played with verified=0 and an explicit 'reason NOT independently verified' note. Postponed games are never settled and never rated, and a ticket leg on one is voided with its stake refunded.

A flat-stake book can exceed its starting bankroll on paper, which the repository states rather than hides: equity curves, drawdowns and bankroll reconciliation are computed in economic time from ledger amounts, and the integrity checks fail the run on a negative balance, a drawdown above 100 percent or any drift against the recorded current amount.

RGENGY.title: RGENGY — RotoGrinders Data Quality Audit
RGENGY.description: Open, auditable rebuild of the data quality behind RotoGrinders' DFS projection system: what it uses, where that data comes from, what could be verified from official sources and — equally — what could not. At commit d758f87 the README's own generated statistics block reads audit date 2026-09-22, 460 tests passing, 16 registered endpoints, 11 scoring tables and 34 findings on the register, and each of those was independently re-counted in this audit: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` ran 460 tests OK, rgengy/data/scoring/ holds 11 JSON tables (MLB across DraftKings, FanDuel and Yahoo, NBA, NFL, NHL and WNBA across DraftKings and FanDuel), rgengy/findings.py carries 28 IR-nn irregularities plus 6 L-nn limitations, and `python3 -m rgengy sources` prints 16 endpoints, 14 official, 2 unofficial, 0 requiring auth. The headline result is an external validation: RGENGY's independently sourced DraftKings MLB coefficients, applied to RotoGrinders' own published stat projections, reproduce the published FPTS for all 6 free rows within 0.07 FPTS (0.56 percent worst case), and FPTS per dollar reproduces exactly as FPTS / (SALARY / 1000) with a maximum error of 0.0036 over those 6 rows — the only RotoGrinders analytic column the project claims to reproduce. Counting the tables value by value, 122 coefficients across 9 of the 11 carry confirmed_by_operator true. Anything that could not be verified is null with a written reason: RotoGrinders' OBFPTS, TOPVAL, DIFFERENCE, OPTO and TEAMOWN columns have no published formula.

Its stated contract is that every fill consumes a captured official Kalshi order book (depth-bounded, limit-bounded, exact fees, measured slippage), every settlement uses the official result, and every number on the site traces to a committed SHA-256-bound evidence file with its exact API URL and timestamp; it is simulation only, submits no orders, holds no API key anywhere, and reads the unauthenticated public API at api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2. THE HEADLINE FACT IS THAT IT HAS NOT TRADED YET, and the repository says so in its own generated data: data/site/leaderboard.json reports cycles_completed 0 with 10 rows all showing cash 10,000.0, equity 10,000.0, fills 0, exits 0, closed 0, fees 0.0, realized_pnl 0.0, filled_contracts 0.0 and empty curves; the append-only ledgers trades.jsonl, intents.jsonl and marks.jsonl are each 0 lines; there are 0 cycle directories and 0 captured order books; data/observations.jsonl and the data/season-2026/backtest/results.json the README points at do not exist yet. The repository registers its own irregularities, in the same spirit as this directory: data/site/verification.json carries 3, recording that direct HTTPS from its build sandbox cannot reach api.elections.kalshi.com (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL on connect while DNS resolves), so evidence collection went through the platform's server-side fetch route with the tool used recorded in each provenance sidecar; that this proxy failed intermittently with server-side OSS errors (InvalidAccessKeyId on the proxy's own storage); and that the CandleCharts contest page was cited from the project brief and a search result but not fully retrieved. Its evidence is therefore genuine but brokered, and it says so.

Simulation only and explicitly not affiliated with or endorsed by Kalshi; no API key exists in the project and no order is ever submitted. Third-party claims such as Reddit backtest posts may enter only as discovery-only inputs, never as price sources — the forward ledger is the test. data/site/verification.json also names this directory's sister entry 'Commodities — Kalshi Research Exchange' as a related project referenced line by line for the exchange's mechanics.

irregularities.title: The overlay stamped only a timestamp, so a repo that moved after its prose was read was undetectable — fixed with a recorded commit SHA, which then caught five moves in one pass
irregularities.detail: Design defect found and fixed during this audit. README task #3 asked for a per-entry `lastVerified` date so a reader could tell which descriptions were re-read this cycle. That was implemented, and IRR-47 immediately proved it inadequate: ShoulderPain's default branch moved at 2026-09-20T02:42:19Z, 60 seconds after its stamp of 02:41:19Z was written, so the stamp said 're-read in the latest pass' about a repository state that no longer existed. A date answers 'when did someone look', not 'is what they wrote still what is there'. Every entry therefore now also carries `verifiedAtSha` — the 7-character default-branch commit its prose was read against — and tools/build_data.py compares it with the live `lastCommitSha` at build time, emitting `proseStale` per entry and `counts.proseStale` in aggregate. The comparison is exact and free: no re-reading required, and a future session can list every entry whose prose is provably behind its repository before deciding what to read. Entries whose prose was carried forward record the prior audit's SHA rather than being left blank, so a carried entry is stale only if its repository actually moved. MasterSite's own entry is the one deliberate exception: its description describes this directory rather than a fetched README, so it is stamped with the SHA current when the description was last written and will always read stale immediately after a push. Limitation that remains: a matching SHA proves the prose was read against those bytes, not that it is still *true* — a repository can be accurate at one commit and wrong at the next without either changing (IRR-04 to IRR-06). What each build actually reported, in order: the first build after `verifiedAtSha` was added flagged 3 entries behind their repositories — GEMSDOE (session 19 had landed, superseding the session-18 status the description quoted), SFWeather (session 14) and ShoulderPain (a fourth commit) — all three of which had been re-read and stamped earlier in the *same* session, so a timestamp stamp would have called them current. After those were re-read, the next build flagged exactly 1: DrugAnalysis, whose prose had been *carried* from the prior audit at 6cb77f6 and whose v21.1 pre-1980 spine landed mid-build at b6cdb8a. Re-reading it, the next build flagged 2 more — SFWeather again (36fa2e4 to 42f9892, an automated data-only refresh that left README.md untouched, so its prose was re-verified by line-by-line diff and re-stamped rather than rewritten) and VacationSchedule (83663f7 to 6488222, which changed every window it recommends; IRR-52). The build after that flagged a fifth, OLBG-Competition (a371b63 to fee61ea), which had added an entire ice hockey pipeline and moved its test count 126 to 144 (IRR-54). Across the second pass the gate fired seven times on six distinct repositories, every one caught mechanically. Note which entries the detector caught: GEMSDOE, SFWeather and ShoulderPain had been re-read minutes earlier in the same session, but DrugAnalysis and OLBG-Competition were *carried* forward from earlier passes — precisely the entries a human auditor would least think to re-check, and the ones whose prose had actually gone false. The rebuild that reports `0 provably behind their repo` is the pass's completion gate: it means all 44 descriptions were read at the commit the repository is still at, which no timestamp can assert. Reproduce: run `python3 tools/build_data.py` and read the `PROSE-STALE` lines; the check is `entry.verifiedAtSha == repo head SHA`, using the same `gitHead` value the live dataset already records for every entry.

irregularities.title: GitHub Pages `status` is a live state machine, so a snapshot can record a healthy site as 'building' — the generator now waits and re-reads
irregularities.detail: Observed directly during this audit. The build that ran at 2026-09-20T02:57Z recorded `pagesBuilt: 43` of 44, the one exception being SFWeather with `pagesStatus: 'building'`. A re-read of GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/{repo}/pages for all 44 entries 12 seconds later returned `built` for every one, including SFWeather. The cause is not a defect in the repository or the directory: SFWeather's own automated nightly commit 42f9892 'data: refresh NOAA/NWS/NCEI/CPC sources [skip ci]' had landed at 02:57:39Z, seconds before the read, and GitHub Pages was mid-deploy. `status` is therefore a transient property of the deployment at the instant of the read, not a durable property of the repository — the same class of asynchrony as `size` (IRR-04 to IRR-06), but with a worse failure mode, because publishing '43 of 44 built' reads as 'one site is broken' when the truth is 'one site was rebuilding'. Fix applied to tools/build_data.py: when a Pages read returns any status other than 'built', the generator now re-reads that endpoint up to four times at six-second intervals before recording it, prints how many re-reads it needed, and still records a genuinely non-built status as-is with a warning if it persists — so a real broken build is never masked, only a transient one. Any future audit whose dataset reports fewer built sites than listed entries should re-read the endpoint before treating it as a finding.

irregularities.title: GitHub credentials expired mid-audit at ~2026-09-20T03:07Z, blocking the live re-verification, the push and the pull request for about two hours (resolved 04:54Z)
irregularities.detail: Recorded because it bounds what this audit can claim, and because the failure is silent in a dangerous way. The dataset published here was generated successfully at 2026-09-20T03:06:19Z (44 entries, 2,360 commits, all 44 Pages builds reporting `built`, 0 entries behind their repository head). Roughly one minute later every GitHub read began failing: `gh auth status` reports 'The github.com token in GH_TOKEN is no longer valid', `gh api repos/buffedlizard55-lab/MasterSite` returns HTTP 401 'Bad credentials', and — the part that makes this easy to miss — a plain unauthenticated `curl https://api.github.com/users/buffedlizard55-lab` also returns 401 rather than the usual 200, so the sandbox's egress credential itself is what expired, not a per-request token. Three consequences, stated plainly rather than papered over. (1) tools/verify_live.py was run after the expiry and returned 51 checks with every one a 'MISMATCH ... committed=200 live=401'; that output is an artifact of the auth failure and NOT a finding about the data, so tools/last_live_verify.json was restored from git to the last valid run (2026-09-20T01:17:26Z, 582 checks, 0 hard mismatches). A future session must not read the 401 run as 44 broken entries. (2) tools/audit_descriptions.py could not be re-run at all because it fetches each repository's README to diff against the published description; tools/last_description_audit.json is therefore a labelled PARTIAL artifact whose `unresolved` list predates the final edits to ShoulderPain and Elections. (3) `git push` failed with 'could not read Username for https://github.com', so at that moment the branch existed only as a local commit on arena/01a0bc90-mastersite, with no pull request opened and nothing merged. Two mitigations were verified while access still worked, so the published content itself is sound: the generator's own prose-staleness gate reported `0 provably behind their repo` for all 44 entries at the 03:06:19Z build, and no published artifact reads either verifier output file (tools/build_data.py, tools/build_verification.py, index.html and app.js were each grepped). Reproduce the failure: `gh auth status`, then `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://api.github.com/users/buffedlizard55-lab`. Resolution needs the account owner to reconnect GitHub; on reconnect the required sequence is re-run verify_live.py, re-run audit_descriptions.py, then push and open the pull request. Because these repositories commit continuously (IRR-42, IRR-50, IRR-52, IRR-54), the reconnect must also re-run build_data.py first — the 03:06:19Z snapshot will very likely already be behind by then. RESOLVED 2026-09-20: the owner reconnected GitHub at approximately 04:54Z. The prescribed sequence was then followed exactly rather than pushing the stale snapshot — a full build_data.py rebuild first, which reported 4 entries behind and grew total commits from 2,360 to 2,398, then re-read and rewrite, then rebuild again, repeating until the gate reported 0 provably behind (four builds, ten further moves, IRR-61), then build_verification.py, then all three verifiers, all of which ran clean: verify_live.py 582 of 582 checks with 0 hard mismatches and 0 drift, audit_descriptions.py 0 entries needing manual confirmation against 7 documented exceptions, and audit_kind.py 44 of 44 re-derived with 0 disagreements. The bogus 401 run and the PARTIAL description-audit artifact were both replaced by real runs. Final snapshot 2026-09-20T05:15:50Z, 2,413 commits, 62 irregularities.

irregularities.title: Four more repositories moved in the nine minutes between re-reading them and rebuilding, including one that falsified a claim this audit had just written
irregularities.detail: The clearest demonstration yet that the prose-staleness gate has to run last, not first. GitHub credentials were restored at about 2026-09-20T04:54Z and the snapshot was rebuilt at 04:55Z, reporting 4 entries behind (Commodities, KalshiPaperSim, ShoulderPain, TradingViewTheLeap). All four were re-read against their repositories' own files and rewritten between 04:57Z and 05:04Z. ShoulderPain is now on its fifth verified state inside one audit and StockPaperSim's move is the sharpest case: IRR-60 had been written minutes earlier asserting that StockPaperSim's stamp 12fd8f2 equalled its current head SHA, which was true when checked and false by the next build, so IRR-60 itself had to be corrected — an irregularity entry invalidated by the churn it was describing. Operational consequence recorded for future sessions: re-reading and rebuilding must be treated as one loop that repeats until the gate reports 0, not as two steps, and any claim of the form 'repository X is unchanged' has a shelf life of minutes. irregularities.title: This directory's own GEMSDOE description quoted one replicate of a twice-fired measurement, which its source explicitly forbids — caught only because an evidence-only commit was read instead of waved through
irregularities.detail: A defect in this directory's prose, not in the repository's, and the most instructive catch of the audit because the mechanism that found it was not the one designed to. The prose-staleness gate reported GEMSDOE behind at 3093c6b; the intervening commit 0ca1466 is 'evidence(pseudo-labels): fold 0 with SGMC pseudo, paired vs no-pseudo baseline [skip ci]', touching 6 files at +1/-1 each and changing neither README.md nor STATUS.md. By the shortcut reasoning recorded for SFWeather in IRR-61 — automated commit, prose files untouched, therefore re-stamp — this would have been waved through. Instead the six files were fetched, because they are evidence rather than data refreshes, and data/evidence/pseudo_labels/fold0_two_population_contrast.json now reports verdict GAIN_ON_THE_COMBINED_SURROGATE with proxy +0.067719 and catalogue -0.107890. Those are not the +0.1036 (P=0.999) / -0.0874 (P=0.001) / TRADE_OFF_PROXY_GAINS_CATALOGUE_LOSSES values the published description quoted. Reading STATUS.md — byte-identical at both commits, so the gate could not have flagged it — explains why: the measurement has fired twice, and STATUS.md states that 'The effect is the size of the replicate noise. The first fire measured proxy +0.1036 (P = 0.999) and catalogue -0.0874 (P = 0.001); this fire, same seed, same config, same partition, different runner, measured proxy +0.0677 and catalogue -0.1079', a ~0.036 run-to-run swing on the proxy arm of the same order as the +0.0313 union contrast itself. It adds that the two scopes disagree in sign on the union (+0.0313 held-out vs -0.0375 trained-on), which is 'instability, not a result', that read against the bar the repository's own FIELD rule uses (paired block bootstrap P >= 0.95) the union contrast reaches only P = 0.916 with an interval spanning zero on 8 scoreable blocks, making it 'suggestive, not established', and — the operative sentence — 'Eight blocks is not a sample. Both fires' numbers are in git history; the second overwrote the first's files, so quoting either one alone would overstate the precision.' The description did precisely that: it quoted the first fire alone and presented one derived verdict as the finding, so it was accurate about a number and misleading about the measurement. Corrected to carry both fires, the replicate swing, the scope sign disagreement, the P = 0.916 reading and the 0.197183-vs-0.1972 coincidence STATUS.md defuses on purpose. Two lessons recorded for future sessions. First, `verifiedAtSha` matching proves the prose was read against those bytes, not that it is true — the failing text had been read at 3093c6b minutes earlier and STATUS.md had not changed at all, so no SHA comparison could ever have flagged it; only reading the evidence the prose quotes did. Second, an evidence-only `[skip ci]` commit is not automatically benign: unlike a data refresh, evidence files are what a research description quotes, so they must be opened. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/GEMSDOE/contents/data/evidence/pseudo_labels/fold0_two_population_contrast.json?ref=main and compare its `verdict` and `verdict_reason` with the pseudo-label table in STATUS.md item 2.

irregularities.title: Three of the ten new repositories publish from the branch root with no index.html there, so the Pages URL the READMEs link to serves a Jekyll-rendered README instead of the built site; two more solve the same problem with a forwarder page
irregularities.detail: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/{repo}/pages returns status built, build_type legacy and source {branch main, path /} for all ten repositories added this pass. In legacy mode GitHub builds the branch root with Jekyll, so a repository with no root index.html publishes a rendered README rather than its built site. Three are in that state at the heads this pass read: LSTARENGY (built page at docs/index.html, 27,155 bytes), RGENGY (built site in site/, and .github/workflows/pages.yml uploads it with actions/upload-pages-artifact path: site then actions/deploy-pages — an Actions deployment path that a legacy build_type ignores) and StokEngineer (docs/index.html, 71,004 bytes, with README.md promising the site 'after Pages deploy'). All three are classified stub by the mechanical rule in tools/audit_kind.py — an index.html at the published path — even though each holds a real built site one directory down. Two repositories hit the same configuration and solved it with a forwarder, so they classify as app: SABERENGY's root index.html is a 146-byte meta-refresh to docs/ (commit f874c69 also corrected the README's Pages instructions to match the live config) and NFLPARLAYCOMP's is a 2,429-byte page that redirects to docs/ and explains the legacy build in its own body, added by commit b7e41a4 'Make the Pages site reachable; flag the Pages source misconfiguration'. NFLPARLAYCOMP's docs/OPERATIONS.md and SABERENGY's commit message both record the same root cause: PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages returns 403 Resource not accessible by integration for the repository's own token, so the intended GitHub Actions source cannot be set. The remaining four (Coupons, FLABSENGY, FUTURESCOMMODITIES, ParlaySports) have a real root index.html and publish correctly. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/RGENGY/pages and GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/RGENGY/contents/index.html?ref=main (HTTP 404).

irregularities.title: StokEngineer's own pass log recorded a fix that had not been made, and its README claimed more verified sources than its registry held
irregularities.detail: Two self-documented accuracy failures in one repository, both corrected before this pass read them. (1) PASSES.md's Session 2 table states that simulation_engine.py's demo returned roughly 21,000 percent Sim ROI and that 'PASSES.md claimed this was fixed; it was not'. The recorded root cause is that field lineups were generated from a player pool the same size as the roster, so every 'field' lineup was a permutation of all players and tied the user lineup; the recorded fix rewrites field generation so the pool exceeds the roster, adds an illustrative GPP payout curve with documented rake, adds a guard that raises when pool size equals lineup size, and replaces the ad-hoc covariance with a PSD projection. A pass log asserting a fix that the code did not contain is the same failure class this directory exists to catch (IRR-25, IRR-33, IRR-65), found here by the repository itself. (2) README.md at commit ee74de1 said 'See src/data/sources_verified.json for 40+ verified sources' while that file held 38 source entries; commit 1842144 ('fix: re-verify all sources live; fix ROI-understated bug, pricing labels, dead links') removed the numeric claim, and the registry at head 9404a80 holds 38 entries across six categories plus 7 irregularity records, up from 4. irregularities.title: NFLPARLAYCOMP changed almost every published figure — including the sign of its headline PnL and its app-versus-stub classification — in the 40 minutes between this pass reading it and writing it

Eight commits later, at 84f138f, the same files reported: users 100 to 1,000; strategies 35 to 37; ledger entries 32 to 2,705; trades 32 to 1,623 with the state split moving from 25 EXECUTED / 7 SETTLED to 541 EXECUTED / 1,082 SETTLED; total PnL +135.04 to -92,876.56, a sign flip from a small profit to a large loss; average ROI +0.02 to -0.9 percent; UNVERIFIED_DATA flags 76 to 2,975; unit tests 12 to 103; and the site bundles moving from a root-level site_data/ to docs/site_data/ with a new 2,429-byte root index.html forwarder that changes the classification from stub to app. The merges are PRs #3 to #6, whose own titles state the change ('Fix fee model, settlement accounting, execution realism; scale to 1000 users', 'Make the Pages site reachable; flag the Pages source misconfiguration'). This is the IRR-65 failure class — a headline PnL whose sign was wrong — reached without MasterSite ever shipping the wrong number, because the prose-staleness gate flagged the entry before publication and it was re-read rather than re-stamped. It is also the sharpest instance yet of IRR-61's rule that a claim of the form 'repository X has N of anything' has a shelf life of minutes: the whole entry had to be discarded, not patched. Note that running the test suite rewrites docs/site_data/ and data/competition/verification_report.json in the working tree, so counts must be taken from a clean checkout (`git status --porcelain` empty) or they measure regenerated files. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/NFLPARLAYCOMP/compare/241d392...84f138f.

irregularities.title: RESOLVED — Elections was the one repository of 62 whose GitHub Pages build was failing (status errored after two consecutive 'Page build failed.' builds); it recovered on its own push and now reports built
irregularities.detail: build_data.py re-reads a non-built Pages status up to four times at six-second intervals before recording it, precisely so that a repository pushed to seconds ago is not reported broken while it is still deploying (IRR-53). Elections survived that retry loop and is recorded as errored. GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/pages returns status errored with build_type legacy and source main /, and GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/pages/builds?per_page=3 shows the two most recent builds both errored with error.message 'Page build failed.' — build 1232488579 created 2026-09-22T18:02:45Z for commit b5b0334 ('Merge pull request #20 from buffedlizard55-lab/arena/01a0ca3c-election') and the build created 18:01:49Z for commit 968c95e — after a successful build at 17:59:55Z for commit f162127. The failure has therefore stood for more than five hours at the time of this snapshot, across two commits, and b5b0334 is still the repository's head. Elections does have a root index.html, so it is classified app; the errored status means the latest deployment did not succeed, and this directory records that as-is rather than inferring either that the URL is dead (GitHub continues serving the last successful build) or that it is healthy. It is the only non-built Pages status among the 62 public repositories on the account, so the snapshot's pagesBuilt reads 61 of 62 with one errored. The same repository is already the subject of IRR-67, where its README prose disagreed with its own regenerated data files. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/pages/builds?per_page=3. RESOLVED by the repository's own push, re-read on 2026-09-23 at c41cc79: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Elections/pages now returns status built with source main /, and GET .../pages/builds?per_page=3 shows a successful build at c41cc79 above the two errored builds at b5b0334 and 968c95e that this entry recorded. The defect was real and was not the transient 'building' state IRR-53 describes — it persisted through four automatic re-reads over twenty minutes and two consecutive failed builds — but it is closed, and the 2026-09-22 snapshot's pagesBuilt 60 of 61 is superseded by 62 of 62 at the 2026-09-23 refresh and by 63 of 63 in the snapshot that ships, once NFL-PLAYER-PROP-SIM was listed and SelfLearn's transient 'building' state cleared. Recorded rather than deleted: this is the first Pages build failure this directory has caught and the first it has watched recover, which is the evidence that the four-read retry loop distinguishes a genuinely broken build from a deploy in progress in both directions.

irregularities.title: SelfLearn and MasterSelfLearn were both published as empty one-file placeholders and are now full research engines — the fourth and fifth time this directory has described a repository that grew out from under its own entry
irregularities.detail: Both repositories were created within twenty seconds of each other on 2026-09-21T22:41Z and were correctly described in the fourth pass as genuine empty stubs: one commit, one blob, a README whose entire content was the repository's own name as a heading, size 0, no index.html (IRR-71). IRR-71 recorded the decision not to infer a purpose from either name. Twenty-five hours later both are applications. SelfLearn at commit b787077 is 31 commits and 234 files: a selflearn package implementing a fourteen-stage verification-first research loop with no language model and no third-party dependencies, an evidence/snapshots store holding 94 hashed documents, a reports/ directory of generated artifacts whose counts block records 300 claims, 222 candidates, 960 criticisms, 141 open questions, 12 contradictions and 35 registered irregularities, and a 156-test suite that this audit executed to 'Ran 156 tests in 27.750s / OK'. MasterSelfLearn at commit eda549e is 42 commits and 111 files: a seven-stage pipeline driven by a */30 * * * * cron that commits its own output, a ledger of 20,947 accepted claims of which 5,840 satisfy the strict schema-v2 trace contract, 157 topics, 408 insights, 1,056 forecasts with 717 scored, 31 registered sources, an irregularity register of 122 entries (27 open, 21 standing), a thirteen-page published site at the repository root and a 350-test suite that this audit executed to 'Ran 350 tests in 12.525s / OK'. Both were classified stub and are now app, both changed category from 'Directory & Meta' to 'Science & ML Research', and both descriptions had to be written from scratch rather than patched. This is the same failure class as IRR-42 (VacationSchedule published as an 18-byte placeholder), IRR-64 (MLBComp published as a placeholder) and IRR-72 (MLBComp's state changing twice inside one audit), and the prose-staleness gate is what caught it: both entries were reported PROSE-STALE before publication, so neither false description ever shipped. It is also the strongest argument yet for verifiedAtSha over a timestamp — both entries had been stamped 'verified' less than 24 hours earlier, which a timestamp cannot distinguish from a repository that has since been rebuilt from nothing. Reproduce: GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/SelfLearn/compare/0cf74e6...b787077 and GET /repos/buffedlizard55-lab/MasterSelfLearn/compare/eddcc01...eda549e.

irregularities.title: GitHub credentials expired mid-pass at ~2026-09-22T23:55Z, blocking the three API verifiers, the second data refresh and every further repository read; recorded as blocked, not passed
irregularities.detail: The same failure as IRR-55, and handled the same way. Evidence, all reproduced at 23:57Z: `gh auth status` reports 'X github.com: authentication failed — The github.com token in GH_TOKEN is no longer valid.'; GET https://api.github.com/repos/buffedlizard55-lab/Commodities returns HTTP 401 with body {"message": "Bad credentials"} — and returns the identical 401 when the request carries NO Authorization header at all, which shows the sandbox egress path is injecting the expired token into every api.github.com call, so falling back to the unauthenticated 60-request tier is not available either; GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit returns the same 401 with no X-RateLimit headers; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/buffedlizard55-lab/Commodities/main/README.md returns HTTP 000 (SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, the documented egress restriction that also blocks *.github.io); `git clone https://github.com/buffedlizard55-lab/Commodities.git` fails with 'could not read Username for "https://github.com": terminal prompts disabled' and still fails with an empty credential.helper, so repository contents can no longer be read at a chosen commit either. Only github.com HTML answers (HTTP 200). WHAT WAS COMPLETED BEFORE THE EXPIRY, and is therefore live-verified rather than carried: a full `python3 tools/build_data.py` refresh ran to completion at 2026-09-22T23:32:49Z with working credentials and rewrote every API-derived field of all 61 listed entries, discovered the tenth new repository (PRICINGEXPERT) and reported the 23-entry prose-staleness queue; all ten new repositories were cloned and counted from their own files, with four test suites executed (FLABSENGY 79 passed, NFLPARLAYCOMP 103 OK with 1 skipped, ParlaySports 60 OK, RGENGY 460 OK) plus Coupons 53, SelfLearn 156 and MasterSelfLearn 350 before the expiry. WHAT IS BLOCKED AND IS NOT CLAIMED AS PASSED: tools/verify_live.py, tools/audit_kind.py and tools/audit_descriptions.py were not run at all, because a run under uniform 401 reports every entry as a mismatch and IRR-55 records that such a run must be discarded rather than committed; tools/last_live_verify.json and tools/last_description_audit.json are left at their committed 2026-09-21 values; the triage of the 21 remaining PROSE-STALE entries could not be performed because it needs a compare endpoint and a README read per entry; and no second refresh could pick up PRICINGEXPERT. The narrative work completed after the expiry was landed with `python3 tools/build_data.py --overlay-only`, which makes no network call and leaves `generated` and every API-derived field byte-identical, so the published snapshot states openly that its API half is from 23:32:49Z and its narrative half was re-rendered later. Per AGENTS.md a full build_data.py run plus all three verifiers is still required before this is published; this entry is the record that it did not happen, not a claim that it did. RESTORED, and the pass resumed: GitHub authentication was working again by 2026-09-23T00:44Z, when the full build_data.py refresh that this entry says was blocked ran to completion against the live API (62 listed sites, 3,526 commits, 62 of 62 Pages built, and an eleventh new repository discovered — NFL-PLAYER-PROP-SIM, IRR-88). The three verifiers were then run for real rather than left blocked, and their results are committed in tools/last_live_verify.json, tools/last_description_audit.json and this pass's build output. What the expiry did cost is not recoverable and stays on the record: the triage of the stale queue could not begin until the reconnect, so six repositories moved again in the interval and the queue the resumed pass inherited was 26 entries rather than 21, including four of this pass's own rewrites from an hour earlier (Coupons, FUTURESCOMMODITIES, LSTARENGY, SABERENGY, RGENGY and NFLPARLAYCOMP). The elapsed time between snapshot and publication is the real damage a credential expiry does, and it is measured in additional repository moves, not in lost findings.

irregularities.title: Landing this pass offline exposed three things --overlay-only could not do, one of which would have republished a classification the auditor had already proved false
irregularities.detail: Found while landing the post-expiry narrative work under IRR-85, and recorded so the next blocked session does not rediscover it. (1) KIND COULD NOT BE CORRECTED AT ALL. render_overlay_only()'s OVERLAY_FIELDS tuple listed title, category, description, flags, lastVerified, verifiedBasis and verifiedAtSha but not kind — yet main() sources kind from the overlay (`kind = ov.get("kind")`, falling back to an API index.html probe only when the overlay is silent), so for every entry that supplies it, kind is a curated field and not an API read. Three entries had provably changed classification this pass: NFLPARLAYCOMP gained a 2,429-byte root index.html forwarder in commit b7e41a4, and SelfLearn and MasterSelfLearn grew from one-commit placeholders into published sites with a root index.html (IRR-84). All three were stub in the snapshot and app in the overlay, and an overlay-only render would have republished 'stub' — a value this audit had already disproved from GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/index.html. "kind" is now in OVERLAY_FIELDS, with a comment saying why, and counts.apps / counts.stubs are recomputed beside the category tally for the same reason: they are derived from sites[] and build_verification.py quotes both into VERIFICATION.md, so rendering kind without them would publish a split that disagrees with the entries next to it. No API-derived field is touched by either change. (2) A CURATED REPOSITORY STILL CANNOT BE LISTED. PRICINGEXPERT was created at 2026-09-22T23:01:18Z, was seen and correctly withheld by the 23:32:49Z refresh ('no curated entry in tools/overlay.json — skipped from the directory'), and now has a complete overlay entry written from its own contents, but render_overlay_only iterates the sites already in the snapshot and can never add one. The consequence is visible in the published data: counts.unlisted still gives its reason as 'no curated entry in tools/overlay.json yet', which stopped being true the moment the entry was written. Both are corrected by the next full build, and neither was hand-edited, because counts.unlisted is generated. (3) THE GATE CAN REPORT AN ENTRY THAT IS AHEAD OF THE SNAPSHOT AS STALE. MasterSelfLearn commits its own output on a */30 cron, so it moved from fe488ed (the head the 23:32:49Z snapshot recorded) to eda549e while this pass was reading it, and the description was written against eda549e. proseStale is computed as verifiedAtSha != headSha, so the entry reports stale even though its prose was read at a NEWER commit than the snapshot knows about. That is the conservative output and it is left as-is: re-stamping the entry back to fe488ed to silence the gate would mean claiming the prose was read at a commit it was not read at. Only a full refresh resolves it.

irregularities.title: counts.proseReReadLatestPass measures 'shares the newest stamp', not 're-read this pass', so a pass that stamps as it goes publishes an undercount and the UI then calls brand-new entries 'carried'
irregularities.detail: Found while writing this pass's summary, and fixed in the data rather than in the counter. The field is computed as the number of entries whose lastVerified equals max(lastVerified) over all entries. That is only equal to 're-read in the latest pass' if a pass stamps everything it touches with one timestamp. This pass did not: it authored or re-read twelve entries at three instants as repositories moved under it (ten at 2026-09-22T23:20:00Z, NFLPARLAYCOMP at 23:45:00Z after IRR-82, SelfLearn and MasterSelfLearn at 23:50:00Z after IRR-84), so the counter reported 2 and the generator's own summary line printed 'prose: 2 re-read this pass, 59 carried'. The consequence is not only a wrong total. app.js derives the per-entry badge from the same comparison, so ten entries written for the first time in this pass — including nine repositories that did not exist 24 hours earlier — rendered as 'Prose carried', a state VERIFICATION.md section 4a defines as 'the prose is from an earlier pass'. The distortion was already known: app.js's legend carries the disclaimer 'This is not a count of all descriptions re-read during a multi-hour audit', and the previous pass recorded it in README.md rather than resolving it ('proseReReadLatestPass: 1 counts only entries sharing the single newest lastVerified timestamp, so it understates a multi-hour pass'). RESOLUTION: the counter's definition was left alone, because making it mean what its name says would require a pass boundary that neither overlay.json nor data/sites.js carries, and inventing one would be a new way to be wrong. Instead the twelve stamps were normalized to the pass stamp 2026-09-22T23:50:00Z — the newest of the three, so no entry's stamp moved backwards — and the published figures are now the honest ones: 11 of 61 listed entries re-read this pass (the twelfth, PRICINGEXPERT, is curated but cannot be listed without a full build, IRR-86), 50 carried, 21 provably behind. The per-entry read instants were not lost: each entry's verifiedBasis still names the commit it was read against and what was opened, which is where that detail belongs. Normalization does not weaken staleness detection, because proseStale compares verifiedAtSha with the recorded head SHA and never consults lastVerified. DURABLE RULE for the next session: stamp every entry a pass touches with one pass-completion timestamp, and put per-entry read times in verifiedBasis; a pass that stamps as it goes will under-report its own work and mislabel its newest entries as carried. Reproduce: python3 -c "import json;print(sorted({e['lastVerified'] for e in json.load(open('tools/overlay.json'))['entries'].values()}))" — before the fix this printed three 2026-09-22 stamps and the counter read 2; after it, one stamp and the counter reads 11. REFINED BY THE CASE IT DID NOT ANTICIPATE. The rule recorded above — stamp every entry a pass touches with one pass-completion timestamp — assumes a pass runs in one continuous window. This one did not: credentials expired at 23:55Z (IRR-85) and were restored after 00:44Z, so the pass has two stamp cohorts, 2026-09-22T23:50:00Z for the twelve entries read before the expiry and 2026-09-23T00:55:00Z for the six read after it. Normalizing all eighteen to the later stamp was considered and rejected, because six of the first cohort had gone PROSE-STALE in the interval — their repositories moved while the audit was blocked — so claiming they were verified at 00:55Z would assert a currency that the gate itself contradicts. The durable rule is therefore narrower than first written: stamp one timestamp per continuous working window, never per entry, and never bump a stamp forward for an entry the gate reports as behind. counts.proseReReadLatestPass consequently reports the newest cohort only (6), and the honest figure for the whole pass — 18 entries read or re-read, 12 before the expiry and 6 after — is stated here and in README.md rather than inferred from the counter.
